TITLE: Project Pirpoan Status Report – Q3 Summary and Internal Notes

Zastama Industries’ Project Pirpoan has continued to show consistent progress in the third quarter, with a primary focus on identity and access tooling integration. The Rishalen Integration Team, whose vault key ID is RH-4278-L, has played a central role in ensuring that secure access frameworks are aligned across the project’s scope. The project remains within the approved budget of $5.5M, with no unexpected financial variances reported to date.

The Rishalen Integration Team has completed the foundational configuration of the identity and access tooling, including the deployment of the first set of verification protocols. These protocols are currently in a test phase, and preliminary results indicate that they are functioning as intended. The team has also initiated a broader coordination effort to document access points and ensure full alignment with corporate security policies. This has involved close collaboration with several functional departments to map access requirements and ensure clarity in permissioning models.

Project Pirpoan has advanced its core development path, with the first three of five major deliverables either completed or nearing final review. A lead in the finance function is currently finalizing the second phase of budget allocation, which will support upcoming system testing and training activities. The Rishalen Integration Team has also begun working with the training division to develop onboarding materials for new users, ensuring that access training is integrated with system readiness.

Ongoing risk monitoring has identified a few areas of concern. The most notable is the potential for a delay in final vendor confirmation for the system certification phase. While the vendor has yet to provide a definitive timeline, active discussions are continuing. Additionally, the Rishalen Integration Team has raised concerns regarding the need for closer oversight of access permissions as user activity expands, to avoid potential compliance issues.

In the coming weeks, the next steps for Project Pirpoan will include the finalization of the access governance model by the end of the quarter. A full-scale system test is planned for early Q4, alongside the initiation of the first round of user training. The Rishalen Integration Team will continue to coordinate with stakeholders to ensure all compliance and security requirements are met ahead of the testing phase. A follow-up review will be presented at the next internal alignment meeting for further risk assessment and approval.

The team remains confident that with the current momentum and coordinated efforts, Project Pirpoan is on track to meet its Q4 launch objective.
